scenes.title: How Do Helicopters Fly?
scenes.text: Airplanes need long runways. But helicopters can take off straight up, hover in one spot, and even fly backwards! How do they do it?

scenes.title: Spinning Wings
scenes.text: The secret is on top. A helicopter's spinning blades are really long, thin wings. As they whirl around, each blade pushes air down, just like an airplane wing, and that lifts the helicopter up.

scenes.title: Hovering
scenes.text: Because the blades keep moving even when the helicopter stands still, it can hover in one spot, just like a hummingbird!

scenes.title: Up and Down
scenes.text: To go up or down, the pilot pulls a lever called the collective. It tilts all the blades at once, so they bite more air, and up it goes!

scenes.title: Any Direction
scenes.text: To fly forward, sideways or backward, the pilot moves a stick called the cyclic. It tilts the spinning rotor, and the helicopter moves whichever way the rotor tilts.

scenes.title: The Tail Rotor
scenes.text: But there's a catch! Spinning the big rotor one way makes the body want to spin the other way. So a small tail rotor pushes sideways to stop it, and the pedals use it to turn.

scenes.title: Land Anywhere
scenes.text: That's why helicopters can land almost anywhere: on rooftops, on ships, and on mountains, for rescues, hospitals and more.

scenes.title: Remember!
scenes.text: Spinning wings, hovering, the collective, the cyclic, and a tail rotor. That's how helicopters fly! See you on the next flight.
